The repair extends its projection requiredness append-only instead of creating a second Native L4 schema.

Existing profile-routed provider lookup with canonical fallback plus the canonical persisted registries. Reused unchanged: the tightened projection flows through the same lookup, and historical canonical readability is preserved by not touching the canonical registry.

Deterministic binder owning the unconditional three-handle-array precondition (the consumer side of the drift). Its local field tuple is hoisted to a module constant so the closure audit reuses it instead of redeclaring the list; binder inference/defaulting semantics are untouched.

Existing single owner for static producer-to-consumer closure with established fail-closed report conventions. Extended in place (unconditional-required extraction, binder-vs-provider subset, enum subset, conditional-rule coverage) rather than creating a second closure auditor or contract registry.

Broadcast (non-profile-dispatched) legacy L4 validation funnel. Profile identity exists only at the persist boundary, so isolation is implemented there with the explicit PROFILE_V21_CATALOG_1 owner; no new context/profile subsystem is created and no duck-typed shape inference is used.

Sanctioned deterministic transformer for the pre-binding closed-corpus path, reachable only through the frozen-manifest validate funnel. Scope-locked with the explicit L4C stage marker (deep_research_run_id) so it cannot become a second writer of bound Fisher candidate state.

Dynamic schema delivery is verified from source and from the real failed-run Fisher prompt file (live v2.1-catalog-1 L4 schema embedded). Prompt prose therefore keeps only scientific decision guidance while the JSON Schema owns machine shape; no prompt-owned schema is created.

Single canonical commit boundary ordering provider validation before deterministic binding before ledger commit. Reused unchanged; the repair only makes the first gate strict enough that incomplete payloads cannot reach the second.

Draft 2020-12 semantics (required vs dependentRequired vs if/then/allOf) already enforced at runtime by the jsonschema dependency. The closure audit mirrors exactly these semantics statically (unconditional vs conditional requirements) instead of adopting a new contract stack.

REUSABLE_COMPONENTS.reason: Would duplicate the JSON-Schema contracts as a second validation owner; explicitly prohibited for this change set.
No new persistence is needed; deltas already persist through schema-validated ledger artifacts. Explicitly prohibited.
SCHEMA_REGISTRY / PROVIDER_SCHEMA_REGISTRY / PERSISTED_SCHEMA_REGISTRY already own registration; explicitly prohibited.
Provider boundary is in-process JSON-Schema validation, not HTTP; adopting a consumer-driven HTTP contract stack would add a parallel owner and new dependencies for no reachable interface.

WHY_NEW_CODE_IS_NECESSARY: No existing owner states the producer-to-consumer guarantee: the provider projection only conditionally required the staged fields while the binder unconditionally demands them, and no static check compared the two. The genuinely new code is therefore (a) append-only requiredness in the existing projection, (b) unconditional-vs-conditional plus enum/conditional-rule comparisons inside the existing closure module reading existing owners, (c) explicit profile gates at the existing persist funnel, (d) a stage-marker scope lock on the existing enricher, and (e) deterministic regression tests including the frozen real Fisher payload. Each is an extension of its owner module, which is why no new registry, model hierarchy, database, framework, or dependency is created.
